Container.Name: messages-server
Container.Overview: Message Link Server keeps your Google Messages, Messenger, Google Voice and Instagram accounts signed in on this server, so the Message Link apps on your PCs and Android phone use them from one place, at home or away through Tailscale.[br][br] [b]Setting up:[/b][br] 1. In Settings, Docker, set Docker Stop Timeout to at least 60 seconds, so messages being sent can finish when the container stops. Then Apply this template.[br] 2. On the Docker tab, open the container's Logs and find the setup code.[br] 3. Open the WebUI. The browser warns about the certificate once, because the server made its own. Enter the setup code and choose the page's password.[br] 4. The page takes you through restoring a backup, your accounts, Tailscale, your phone and PCs, notifications and backups.[br][br] [b]Where things live:[/b] the Docker volumes messages-server-data and messages-server-keys, in Docker's own storage and on none of your shares. Daily backups go to a network share you choose on the server's page (a share on this server works). They hold your history, settings and devices, never a sign-in. The volumes use space in Docker's own storage, so leave room there for your history.[br][br] [b]Chrome's sandbox:[/b] the server shows each service's sign-in in its own Google Chrome, which runs every page in Chrome's sandbox. For that, the container runs without Docker's default system call filter (seccomp=unconfined). It still runs as its own user, with every capability dropped.

Config.Name: Port
Config.Description: The one port the Message Link apps and the server's page use (HTTPS).

Config.Name: Reach from your tailnet
Config.Description: 1 puts the server on your Tailscale network as a machine of its own, so your phone reaches it from anywhere while the port above stays on your home network. The server's page signs it in. 0 turns it off.

Config.Name: Backups folder
Config.Description: Leave empty and choose a network share on the server's page.

Config.Name: Tailscale auth key
Config.Description: Optional: a Tailscale auth key (tskey-auth-...) that signs the server in by itself the first time, instead of the page's sign-in. A tagged key lets in every device your access rules allow, not only your own. Clear it once the server is signed in.

Config.Name: Tailnet name
Config.Description: Optional: the server's name on your Tailscale network: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

Config.Name: Server names
Config.Description: Optional: the names and addresses devices reach the server by, comma-separated, written into its certificate when it is first made (devices trust its fingerprint, not these names).

Config.Name: Server page password
Config.Description: Optional: sets the page's password here instead of on its first visit (12 to 128 characters, used nowhere else). Unraid shows it in the docker command it prints.

Config.Name: Resume sign-ins at start
Config.Description: 1 resumes the accounts signed in on this server when it starts.

Config.Name: Google Messages and Voice
Config.Description: 1 runs Google Messages and Google Voice beside the server's own Google Chrome.

Config.Name: Google through Chrome
Config.Description: Leave at 1: Google is signed in by hand in the server's own Chrome, which keeps the sign-in fresh.

Config.Name: Chrome on its own display
Config.Description: Leave at 1: Chrome draws on a virtual display inside the container.

Config.Name: Network of its own
Config.Description: 1 on the bridge network: the container has a network of its own, so the page may show sign-ins from the server's Chrome. Set 0 with host networking.

Config.Name: Chrome without its sandbox
Config.Description: Leave at 0: Chrome runs every page in its sandbox. 1 turns the sandbox off, and a page that broke out of Chrome could then read every sign-in on this server.

Config.Name: Data folder in the container
Config.Description: Leave as /data, the volume in Extra Parameters.

Config.Name: Keys folder in the container
Config.Description: Leave as /keys, the volume in Extra Parameters.
